attributes.references: Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO); Multiple Listing Service (MLS)

attributes.name: months_of_supply
attributes.description: Estimated number of months it would take to sell all current active listings at the current absorption rate. Less than 3 months indicates a sellers market; more than 6 months indicates a buyers market.
attributes.references: National Association of Realtors (NAR)

attributes.name: pending_comparable_count
attributes.description: Number of pending (under contract) comparable listings included in the analysis. Pending comparables indicate near-term market clearing prices.
attributes.references: National Association of Realtors (NAR); Multiple Listing Service (MLS)

attributes.name: pricing_strategy
attributes.description: The analyst's recommended pricing approach for the listing based on market conditions, seller objectives, and CMA findings. Aggressive pricing targets above-market value; below-market pricing aims for rapid sale.
attributes.references: National Association of Realtors (NAR)

attributes.name: property_type
attributes.description: Classification of the subject property type, which determines the comparable selection methodology and market segment for the CMA. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: single_family|multi_family|condominium|townhouse|commercial|land|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO); National Association of Realtors (NAR)

attributes.name: recommended_list_price
attributes.description: The specific listing price recommended by the analyst based on the CMA findings, market trend assessment, and pricing strategy. Falls within or near the concluded value range.
attributes.references: National Association of Realtors (NAR); Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: report_document_url
attributes.description: URL or file path to the generated CMA report document (PDF or presentation format) stored in the document management system or DocuSign CLM. Supports client delivery and audit trail.
attributes.references: DocuSign CLM

attributes.name: sold_comparable_count
attributes.description: Number of recently sold comparable properties included in the analysis. Sold comparables are the primary evidence of market value in a CMA.
attributes.references: National Association of Realtors (NAR); Multiple Listing Service (MLS)

attributes.name: subject_address
attributes.description: Full street address of the subject property being analyzed. Captured directly on the CMA record for report generation and historical reference independent of the property master record.
attributes.references: Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: subject_city
attributes.description: City in which the subject property is located. Used for market segmentation and comparable search radius definition.
attributes.references: Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: subject_state
attributes.description: Two-letter US state code for the subject property location. Governs applicable real estate licensing and disclosure requirements.
attributes.references: Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO); National Association of Realtors (NAR)

attributes.name: subject_zip
attributes.description: ZIP or postal code of the subject property. Used to define the primary comparable search area and align with MLS market area boundaries.
attributes.references: Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this CMA record was most recently modified. Supports change tracking, data lineage, and audit compliance in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act); FASB ASC 820

products.name: comparable_sale
products.description: Individual comparable sale (comp) record used as evidence in appraisals, BPOs, and CMAs. Stores comp property address, sale date, sale price, price PSF, GLA/NLA, property type, year built, condition, location adjustments, physical adjustments, time adjustments, adjusted sale price, data source (CoStar, MLS, public record), and verification status. Supports the sales comparison approach in USPAP/IVSC-compliant valuations. Sourced from CoStar Suite and MLS data feeds.
products.reference: CoStar Suite — Comparable Sales Database; USPAP Sales Comparison Approach

attributes.name: address_line1
attributes.description: Primary street address of the comparable sale property (street number and street name). Used to identify the physical location of the comp for geographic adjustment analysis.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO); ALTA Survey Standards

attributes.name: address_line2
attributes.description: Secondary address information for the comparable sale property (suite, unit, floor, building name). Supplements the primary address for precise property identification.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: adjusted_price_psf
attributes.description: The adjusted sale price divided by the gross leasable area, expressed as adjusted price per square foot (PSF). The primary reconciled unit-of-comparison metric used to bracket and support the subject property's value conclusion.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: adjusted_sale_price
attributes.description: The comparable sale price after application of all adjustments (location, physical, time, and other). This is the final adjusted value indicator used in the reconciliation of the sales comparison approach to derive the subject property's market value opinion.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; IVSC IVS 105; FASB ASC 820 Fair Value Measurement

attributes.name: appraiser_notes
attributes.description: Free-text narrative notes entered by the appraiser describing the rationale for selecting this comparable, the basis for adjustments applied, and any special circumstances affecting the sale. Required for USPAP Standard 1 documentation of the sales comparison approach.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: arms_length_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the comparable sale was an arm's length transaction between unrelated parties with no undue influence (True) or a non-arm's length transaction (False) such as a foreclosure, related-party sale, or distressed sale. Non-arm's length transactions require additional adjustment or exclusion per USPAP.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; IVSC IVS 105; FASB ASC 820

attributes.name: cap_rate_at_sale
attributes.description: The implied capitalization rate (CAP rate) at the time of the comparable sale, calculated as the net operating income (NOI) divided by the sale price. A key market indicator used in income approach cross-checks and investment analysis.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; Argus Enterprise; IVSC IVS 105; NCREIF

attributes.name: city
attributes.description: City or municipality in which the comparable sale property is located. Used for market area delineation and location adjustment analysis.
attributes.references: Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO); CoStar Suite

attributes.name: comp_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known identifier for this comparable sale record, typically sourced from CoStar Suite, MLS, or public record systems (e.g., CoStar property ID, MLS listing number, or county assessor parcel number).
attributes.references: CoStar Suite; Multiple Listing Service (MLS); Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: condition_rating
attributes.description: Overall physical condition rating of the comparable sale property at the time of sale. Used to determine physical adjustment requirements in the sales comparison approach.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; Fannie Mae Uniform Appraisal Dataset (UAD) Condition Ratings

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this comparable sale record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail and data lineage requirements.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) Section 404; GDPR Article 5 (data integrity); ISO 55000 Asset Management

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Primary source from which the comparable sale data was obtained (e.g., CoStar Suite, MLS data feed, county deed/public record, appraiser files). Supports USPAP verification and data provenance requirements.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO); CoStar Suite

attributes.name: data_source_record_reference
attributes.description: The unique identifier of this comparable sale record within the originating source system (e.g., CoStar property ID, MLS listing number, county assessor parcel number). Enables traceability back to the source system for verification.
attributes.references: CoStar Suite; Multiple Listing Service (MLS); Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: distressed_sale_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the comparable sale was a distressed transaction (True), such as a foreclosure, Real Estate Owned (REO) sale, short sale, or bankruptcy sale. Distressed sales may require exclusion or significant adjustment in USPAP-compliant appraisals.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD); IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: financing_type
attributes.description: Type of financing used in the comparable sale transaction (e.g., conventional mortgage, cash, seller financing, assumed mortgage, CMBS). Atypical financing may require a cash equivalency adjustment per USPAP.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; IVSC IVS 105; Fannie Mae Selling Guide

attributes.name: gla_sqft
attributes.business_glossary_term: Gross Leasable Area in Square Feet (GLA SQF)
attributes.description: Total gross leasable area (GLA) of the comparable sale property measured in square feet (SQF). Primary size metric used to calculate price per square foot (PSF) and to assess comparability with the subject property.
attributes.references: Building Owners and Managers Association (BOMA) Measurement Standards; Appraisal Institute USPAP; Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: location_adjustment_pct
attributes.description: Percentage adjustment applied to the comparable sale price to account for locational differences between the comparable property and the subject property (e.g., submarket quality, access, visibility, corner location). Positive values indicate the subject is superior; negative values indicate the comparable is superior.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; IVSC IVS 105 Valuation Approaches and Methods

attributes.name: lot_size_sqft
attributes.description: Total land area of the comparable sale property parcel measured in square feet. Critical for land valuation, FAR analysis, and comparability assessment for properties where land value is a significant component.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: nla_sqft
attributes.business_glossary_term: Net Leasable Area in Square Feet (NLA SQF)
attributes.description: Net leasable area (NLA) of the comparable sale property measured in square feet, excluding common areas. Used as an alternative unit of comparison for properties where NLA is the market-standard measurement basis.
attributes.references: Building Owners and Managers Association (BOMA) Measurement Standards; Appraisal Institute USPAP

attributes.name: noi_at_sale
attributes.description: The net operating income (NOI) of the comparable property at the time of sale, used to calculate the implied CAP rate and to support income approach cross-validation in the appraisal.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; Argus Enterprise; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: number_of_stories
attributes.description: Total number of above-grade floors or stories in the comparable sale property. Used as a physical characteristic for comparability assessment and adjustment.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; CoStar Suite

attributes.name: occupancy_rate_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of the comparable property that was occupied at the time of sale. Used to assess income-producing capacity and to determine whether occupancy-related adjustments are required.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; CoStar Suite

attributes.name: other_adjustment_pct
attributes.description: Aggregate percentage adjustment for all other factors not captured in location, physical, or time adjustments (e.g., financing concessions, conditions of sale, expenditures made immediately after purchase). Applied per USPAP adjustment methodology.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; IVSC IVS 105; Fannie Mae Selling Guide

attributes.name: parking_spaces
attributes.description: Total number of parking spaces (surface, structured, or underground) associated with the comparable sale property. Used to assess parking ratio and determine parking-related adjustments.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; CoStar Suite

attributes.name: physical_adjustment_pct
attributes.description: Percentage adjustment applied to the comparable sale price to account for physical differences between the comparable and subject property (e.g., size, age, condition, quality, amenities). Positive values indicate the subject is superior.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: postal_code
attributes.description: ZIP or postal code of the comparable sale property location. Used for submarket delineation, geographic clustering, and location adjustment analysis.
attributes.references: Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO); CoStar Suite

attributes.name: price_psf
attributes.description: Sale price divided by the gross leasable area or building area, expressed as price per square foot (PSF). A primary unit-of-comparison metric used in the sales comparison approach for commercial and residential appraisals.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; CoStar Suite; Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: price_psm
attributes.description: Sale price divided by the building area expressed in square meters (SQM). Used for international valuations and IVSC-compliant reporting where metric units are required.
attributes.references: IVSC International Valuation Standards; ISO 80000-3 Quantities and Units

attributes.name: property_subtype
attributes.description: More granular classification of the comparable property within its property type (e.g., Class A Office, Strip Center, Bulk Warehouse, Garden Apartment). Supports refined comparability analysis.
attributes.references: CoStar Suite; Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: quality_rating
attributes.description: Rating of the construction quality and finish level of the comparable sale property. Used to assess quality-based adjustments in the sales comparison approach.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; Fannie Mae Uniform Appraisal Dataset (UAD) Quality Ratings

attributes.name: sale_date
attributes.description: The date on which the comparable property sale was recorded or closed, used as the principal business event date for time adjustment calculations in the sales comparison approach.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; IVSC IVS 105; FASB ASC 820

attributes.name: sale_price
attributes.description: The gross transaction price at which the comparable property sold, expressed in the local currency. This is the unadjusted arm's-length sale price as recorded in deed or public record.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; IVSC IVS 105; FASB ASC 820 Fair Value Measurement

attributes.name: state_province
attributes.description: State, province, or territory in which the comparable sale property is located. Used for jurisdictional market analysis and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO); National Association of Realtors (NAR)

attributes.name: time_adjustment_pct
attributes.description: Percentage adjustment applied to the comparable sale price to account for market conditions changes between the comparable sale date and the effective appraisal date. Reflects market appreciation or depreciation over the intervening period.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; IVSC IVS 105; FASB ASC 820

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this comparable sale record was most recently modified, supporting audit trail, data lineage, and change tracking requirements.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) Section 404; GDPR Article 5 (data integrity); ISO 55000 Asset Management

attributes.name: verification_date
attributes.description: The date on which the comparable sale data was verified against the primary source. Supports USPAP compliance documentation and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: verification_method
attributes.description: The method used to verify the accuracy of the comparable sale data (e.g., public deed record, direct buyer/seller confirmation, broker confirmation, CoStar verification). Required by USPAP Standard 1 for sales comparison approach documentation.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: verification_status
attributes.description: Current verification status of the comparable sale record indicating whether the sale data has been confirmed against primary sources (deed records, CoStar, MLS, or direct buyer/seller confirmation) per USPAP verification requirements.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: year_built
attributes.description: The calendar year in which the comparable sale property was originally constructed. Used to assess age-related physical depreciation and comparability with the subject property.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; CoStar Suite; Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

products.name: comparable_lease

Supports market rent conclusions in income approach valuations.

attributes.name: adjusted_rent_psf
attributes.description: Base rent per square foot after applying all grid adjustments (time, location, condition, size, etc.) to normalize the comparable lease to the subject property characteristics. The final adjusted rent used in market rent conclusions.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; International Valuation Standards Council (IVSC) IVS 105

attributes.name: analyst_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for appraiser or analyst commentary on the comparable lease, including any unusual terms, market conditions at time of execution, or qualitative factors affecting comparability. Supports USPAP narrative appraisal report requirements.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; USPAP; International Valuation Standards Council (IVSC) IVS 105

attributes.name: base_rent_psf
attributes.description: Annual base rent expressed on a per-square-foot (PSF) basis for the comparable lease. The primary rent metric used in income capitalization and market rent conclusions. Classified as confidential due to commercially sensitive deal terms.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; International Valuation Standards Council (IVSC) IVS 105; CoStar Suite

attributes.name: cam_charges_psf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Common Area Maintenance Charges Per Square Foot (CAM PSF)
attributes.description: Common Area Maintenance (CAM) charges expressed on a per-square-foot annual basis for the comparable lease. Used to gross up NNN rents to a gross equivalent for cross-lease comparisons.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: city
attributes.description: City in which the comparable property is located. Used for geographic market segmentation and submarket assignment.
attributes.references: Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: comp_property_address
attributes.description: Full street address of the comparable property including street number, street name, suite or floor where applicable. Used for geographic proximity analysis in market rent conclusions.
attributes.references: Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO); ALTA

attributes.name: comp_property_name
attributes.description: Common or marketing name of the comparable property (e.g., 'One Embarcadero Center', 'Westfield Mall'). Used for identification and reporting in valuation narratives.
attributes.references: CoStar Suite; Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: comp_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known identifier or deal reference number assigned to this comparable lease transaction, as sourced from CoStar, MLS, or direct broker confirmation. Serves as the business-facing unique code for the comp record.
attributes.references: CoStar Suite; Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: condition_adjustment_pct
attributes.description: Percentage adjustment applied to the comparable lease rent to account for differences in building condition, quality, or finish level between the comparable and subject properties.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; International Valuation Standards Council (IVSC) IVS 105

attributes.name: costar_property_reference
attributes.description: CoStar Suite's unique property identifier for the comparable property. Enables direct cross-reference to CoStar market data for automated comp retrieval and market analytics.
attributes.references: CoStar Suite

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Primary source from which the comparable lease transaction data was obtained (e.g., CoStar Suite, MLS, direct landlord/tenant confirmation, broker, public record). Determines the reliability tier of the comp in IVSC-compliant methodology documentation.
attributes.references: International Valuation Standards Council (IVSC) IVS 105; Appraisal Institute

attributes.name: effective_rent_psf
attributes.description: Net effective rent per square foot after accounting for free rent periods, tenant improvement allowances, and other landlord concessions amortized over the lease term. Provides a true economic rent comparison across leases with varying concession packages.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; International Valuation Standards Council (IVSC) IVS 105

attributes.name: expansion_option_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the comparable lease includes a tenant expansion option for additional space. Relevant for assessing tenant demand and flexibility provisions in market analysis.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: free_rent_months
attributes.description: Number of months of rent abatement (free rent) granted to the tenant at lease commencement. A landlord concession that reduces effective rent; used to normalize comparable leases to a common economic basis.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; International Valuation Standards Council (IVSC) IVS 105

attributes.name: lease_commencement_date
attributes.description: Date on which the comparable lease term officially commenced and the tenant took occupancy or began paying rent. Used to determine the effective market date and calculate free rent periods.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 842; IASB IFRS 16

attributes.name: lease_execution_date
attributes.description: Date on which the comparable lease agreement was fully executed (signed) by both landlord and tenant. Establishes the market date for the transaction, critical for time-adjustment analysis in income approach valuations.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 842; IASB IFRS 16; Appraisal Institute

attributes.name: lease_expiration_date
attributes.description: Scheduled expiration date of the comparable lease term. Used in conjunction with commencement date to validate the stated lease term in months.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 842; IASB IFRS 16

attributes.name: lease_size_sqf
attributes.description: Total leased area of the comparable lease expressed in square feet (SQF). Used to assess scale comparability with the subject property and to weight rent conclusions in market analysis.
attributes.references: Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO); Appraisal Institute

attributes.name: lease_size_sqm
attributes.description: Total leased area of the comparable lease expressed in square meters (SQM). Used for international market comparisons and IVSC-compliant valuation reports.
attributes.references: International Valuation Standards Council (IVSC); Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: lease_term_months
attributes.description: Total duration of the comparable lease expressed in months from commencement to expiration. A key comparability factor in market rent analysis; longer terms typically command lower effective rents.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; International Valuation Standards Council (IVSC) IVS 105

attributes.name: location_adjustment_pct
attributes.description: Percentage adjustment applied to the comparable lease rent to account for locational differences between the comparable and subject properties. Part of the grid adjustment methodology in income approach valuations.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; International Valuation Standards Council (IVSC) IVS 105

attributes.name: operating_expense_stop_psf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Operating Expense Stop Per Square Foot (PSF)
attributes.description: Base year operating expense stop per square foot above which the tenant is responsible for expense increases. Common in modified gross leases; used to normalize rent comparisons across different expense structures.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; FASB ASC 842

attributes.name: postal_code
attributes.description: Postal or ZIP code of the comparable property location. Supports geographic clustering and submarket boundary analysis.
attributes.references: Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: property_class
attributes.description: Building quality classification of the comparable property (Class A, B, or C) based on age, condition, amenities, and location. Used to ensure comparability with the subject property in rent analysis.
attributes.references: Urban Land Institute (ULI); CoStar Suite

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this comparable lease record was first created in the system. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and Silver layer ingestion tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act); ISO 55000 Asset Management

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this comparable lease record was last modified. Supports change tracking, data quality monitoring, and audit trail requirements in the Silver layer.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act); ISO 55000 Asset Management

attributes.name: renewal_option_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the comparable lease includes one or more tenant renewal options. Presence of renewal options affects the economic value of the lease and is noted in market rent analysis.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; FASB ASC 842

attributes.name: renewal_option_term_months
attributes.description: Duration in months of each renewal option period available to the tenant under the comparable lease. Used to assess the total potential lease commitment and WALT calculations.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; FASB ASC 842

attributes.name: rent_escalation_rate
attributes.description: Annual rent escalation rate expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.03 for 3%) applicable to fixed or percentage-based escalation structures. Used in Argus Enterprise DCF models to project future rent cash flows.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise; Appraisal Institute

attributes.name: rent_escalation_type
attributes.description: Method by which base rent escalates over the lease term (e.g., fixed annual percentage, CPI-linked, stepped increases, or flat). Used to assess the economic profile of the comparable lease in DCF-based valuation models.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; Argus Enterprise

attributes.name: state_province
attributes.description: State or province in which the comparable property is located. Used for regulatory jurisdiction mapping and geographic market analysis.
attributes.references: Real Estate Standards Organization (RESO)

attributes.name: ti_allowance_psf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Tenant Improvement Allowance Per Square Foot (TI PSF)
attributes.description: Tenant Improvement (TI) allowance provided by the landlord expressed on a per-square-foot basis. A key concession metric used to normalize comparable leases and assess true economic rent in income approach valuations.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; FASB ASC 842; CoStar Suite

attributes.name: time_adjustment_pct
attributes.description: Percentage adjustment applied to the comparable lease rent to account for market conditions between the lease execution date and the valuation date. Used in the sales comparison and income approaches to normalize historical comps to current market.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; International Valuation Standards Council (IVSC) IVS 105

attributes.name: verification_date
attributes.description: Date on which the comparable lease transaction data was verified through a reliable source. Required for IVSC-compliant methodology documentation and appraisal report quality control.
attributes.references: International Valuation Standards Council (IVSC) IVS 105; Appraisal Institute

attributes.name: verification_status
attributes.description: Current verification state of the comparable lease data indicating whether the transaction details have been confirmed through a reliable source such as broker confirmation, public record, or direct tenant/landlord contact. Drives reliability weighting in rent analysis.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; International Valuation Standards Council (IVSC) IVS 105

products.name: approach
products.description: Valuation approach model record capturing the quantitative analysis for income capitalization and cost approach methodologies. For income capitalization: stores PGI, vacancy/credit loss rate, EGI, total OPEX, NOI, CAP rate, direct capitalization value, terminal CAP rate, discount rate, hold period, IRR/NPV outputs, and concluded market rent inputs. For cost approach: stores land value, replacement cost new (RCN), depreciation components (physical, functional, external obsolescence), depreciated cost of improvements, effective age, economic life, and cost index source (Marshall & Swift, RSMeans). Includes approach type discriminator (direct_cap, DCF, cost, sales_comparison, GRM) and approach weight in final reconciliation. Supports IVSC IVS 105 compliance. After merge with cost_approach, this is the unified approach model for all valuation methodologies.
products.reference: Argus Enterprise — DCF Model; IVSC IVS 105 Income Approach

attributes.name: approach_id
attributes.description: Primary key for approach

attributes.name: appraisal_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent valuation engagement or appraisal report to which this approach record belongs. Links the approach to its overarching valuation assignment.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 101 — Scope of Work; Appraisal Institute USPAP

attributes.name: appraiser_id
attributes.description: Reference to the certified appraiser responsible for preparing and signing off on this valuation approach. Links to the appraiser credential record capturing Appraisal Institute certification, state license, and USPAP compliance status.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — Appraiser Credentials; USPAP Ethics Rule; IVSC IVS 101

attributes.name: asset_id
attributes.description: Reference to the subject property being valued under this approach. Ties the valuation approach to the specific real estate asset in the property master record.
attributes.references: RESO Data Dictionary; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: cap_rate_benchmark_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to valuation.cap_rate_benchmark. Business justification: valuation_approach uses cap_rate in direct capitalization. The applied cap rate should be benchmarked against market data. Adding cap_rate_benchmark_id links the approach model to the market benchmark

attributes.name: currency_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.currency_code. Business justification: Valuation approach financial outputs (concluded_value, pgi, egi, noi, land_value, replacement_cost_new) are currency-denominated. Normalizing to a FK enables consistent currency handling in multi-curr
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the supervising appraiser or peer reviewer who reviewed and approved this valuation approach. Supports quality control workflows and USPAP Standard 3 (Appraisal Review) compliance.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 3 — Appraisal Review; IVSC IVS 101

attributes.name: noi_statement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.noi_statement. Business justification: The income approach in valuation_approach uses NOI as its primary input. Linking to the authoritative NOI statement documents the source of the NOI figure used in the income approach, supporting USPAP
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: property_type_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.property_type. Business justification: Valuation approach parameters (cap rate, GRM, cost indices, depreciation rates) are property-type-specific. A domain expert would expect the income, sales comparison, and cost approaches to reference
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: approach_date
attributes.description: Effective date as of which the valuation approach analysis is performed. Represents the appraisal effective date for this specific methodology, which may differ from the report date.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 101 — Scope of Work; USPAP Standards Rule 1-2(b)

attributes.name: approach_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of this valuation approach record within the appraisal workflow. Tracks progression from initial draft through peer review, approval, and potential supersession by a revised approach.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 101 — Scope of Work; Appraisal Institute USPAP

attributes.name: approach_type
attributes.description: Discriminator identifying the valuation methodology applied in this record. Supported types: direct_cap (Direct Capitalization), DCF (Discounted Cash Flow), cost (Cost Approach), sales_comparison (Sales Comparison Approach), GRM (Gross Rent Multiplier). Drives which set of methodology-specific fields are populated.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105 — Valuation Approaches and Methods; Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1

attributes.name: approved_date
attributes.description: Date on which this valuation approach was formally approved by the reviewing appraiser or valuation committee. Marks the transition from in_review to approved status in the approach lifecycle.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP; IVSC IVS 101 — Scope of Work

attributes.name: argus_model_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier or file path for the Argus Enterprise cash flow model associated with this DCF valuation approach. Enables traceability back to the source Argus model for audit, review, and replication purposes. Populated for DCF approach type.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise — Valuation and Cash Flow Modeling; IVSC IVS 101 — Scope of Work

attributes.name: cap_rate
attributes.description: Overall capitalization rate (CAP rate) applied to stabilized NOI to derive the direct capitalization value. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0550 = 5.50%). Derived from market comparable sales analysis and reflects investor return expectations for the asset class and submarket.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, 15th Ed.; IVSC IVS 105; CoStar Market Analytics

attributes.name: comparable_count
attributes.description: Number of comparable sales or lease transactions used to support the approach inputs (e.g., CAP rate derivation for direct cap, market rent for income approaches, adjusted sales for sales comparison). Indicates the depth of market evidence supporting the concluded value.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1; IVSC IVS 105; CoStar Comparable Data

attributes.name: concluded_market_rent_psf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Concluded Market Rent Per Square Foot (PSF)
attributes.description: Appraiser's concluded market rent per square foot (PSF) used as the basis for PGI estimation in income capitalization approaches. Derived from comparable lease analysis and market surveys. Expressed in the reporting currency per square foot per year.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, 15th Ed.; RESO Data Dictionary; CoStar Comparable Lease Data

attributes.name: concluded_value
attributes.description: The indicated market value produced by this specific valuation approach before reconciliation weighting. Represents the raw output of the methodology (e.g., direct capitalization value, DCF NPV, depreciated cost, or sales comparison adjusted value) in the reporting currency.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105; FASB ASC 820 — Fair Value Measurement

attributes.name: cost_index_source
attributes.description: Source of the construction cost index or cost manual used to estimate RCN in the cost approach. Common sources include Marshall & Swift Valuation Service and RSMeans Cost Data. Supports methodology transparency and IVSC IVS 105 compliance documentation.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105 — Cost Approach; Marshall & Swift Valuation Service; RSMeans Cost Data

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp recording when this valuation approach record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and SOX financial controls for valuation records used in financial reporting.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 — Internal Controls; FASB ASC 820; GDPR Article 5 — Data Integrity

attributes.name: depreciated_cost_of_improvements
attributes.description: Net value of the improvements after deducting total accrued depreciation (physical, functional, and external obsolescence) from RCN. Added to land value to derive the cost approach indicated value. Populated for cost approach type.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105 — Cost Approach; Appraisal Institute USPAP

attributes.name: direct_cap_value
attributes.description: Indicated value derived by dividing stabilized NOI by the overall CAP rate (NOI / CAP Rate). Represents the concluded value under the direct capitalization method. Populated only when approach_type = direct_cap.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, 15th Ed.; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: discount_rate
attributes.description: Risk-adjusted discount rate (expressed as a decimal) used in the DCF analysis to convert projected future cash flows to present value. Reflects the required rate of return for the investment, incorporating market risk, asset type, and leverage. Populated for DCF approach type.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105; Argus Enterprise DCF Methodology; Appraisal Institute

attributes.name: economic_life_years
attributes.description: Total estimated economic life of the improvements in years — the period over which the building is expected to contribute positively to property value. Used with effective age to calculate the age-life depreciation ratio in the cost approach.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105 — Cost Approach; Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, 15th Ed.

attributes.name: effective_age_years
attributes.description: Appraiser's estimate of the effective age of the improvements in years, reflecting the actual condition and utility of the building relative to a new structure of similar type. May differ from chronological age due to renovations or deferred maintenance. Used in cost approach depreciation calculations.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105 — Cost Approach; Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, 15th Ed.

attributes.name: egi
attributes.description: Effective Gross Income — PGI adjusted for vacancy, credit loss, and other income (e.g., parking, ancillary revenue). Represents the realistic annual income the property is expected to generate. Populated for direct_cap and DCF approach types.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, 15th Ed.; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: external_obsolescence
attributes.description: Loss in value caused by factors external to the property, such as adverse market conditions, neighborhood decline, or proximity to negative influences. Also known as economic obsolescence. Deducted from RCN in the cost approach.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105 — Cost Approach; Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, 15th Ed.

attributes.name: functional_obsolescence
attributes.description: Loss in value resulting from deficiencies or superadequacies in the design, layout, or functionality of the improvements relative to current market standards (e.g., outdated floor plans, inadequate HVAC systems). Deducted from RCN in the cost approach.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105 — Cost Approach; Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, 15th Ed.

attributes.name: grm
attributes.description: Gross Rent Multiplier — the ratio of property value to gross annual (or monthly) rental income, derived from comparable sales. Applied to the subject property's gross rent to estimate value under the GRM approach. Populated when approach_type = GRM.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, 15th Ed.; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: hold_period_years
attributes.description: Projected investment hold period in years used in the DCF analysis. Defines the number of annual cash flow periods modeled before the terminal reversion value is calculated. Typically ranges from 5 to 15 years for commercial real estate. Populated for DCF approach type.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105; Argus Enterprise DCF Methodology

attributes.name: irr
attributes.description: Internal Rate of Return — the discount rate at which the net present value of all projected cash flows (including acquisition cost and terminal reversion) equals zero. Key investment performance metric output from the DCF model. Populated for DCF approach type.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105; Argus Enterprise; CFA Institute — Real Estate Valuation

attributes.name: ivsc_methodology_code
attributes.description: IVSC IVS 105 methodology classification code identifying the specific valuation technique applied (e.g., IVS105-IC for Income Capitalization, IVS105-CA for Cost Approach, IVS105-SC for Sales Comparison). Supports regulatory compliance documentation and cross-border reporting.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105 — Valuation Approaches and Methods

attributes.name: land_value
attributes.description: Estimated market value of the land component as if vacant and available for its highest and best use. Used in the cost approach as the foundation to which depreciated cost of improvements is added. Populated for cost approach type.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105 — Cost Approach; Appraisal Institute USPAP

attributes.name: methodology_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field capturing appraiser commentary on the rationale, assumptions, limitations, and adjustments specific to this valuation approach. Supports IVSC IVS 105 compliance, USPAP disclosure requirements, and peer review documentation.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105; Appraisal Institute USPAP Standards Rule 2-2; FASB ASC 820

attributes.name: noi
attributes.description: Net Operating Income — EGI minus total OPEX. The primary income metric used in direct capitalization and DCF valuation. Represents the annual pre-debt, pre-tax cash flow generated by the property. Populated for direct_cap and DCF approach types.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, 15th Ed.; IVSC IVS 105; FASB ASC 820

attributes.name: npv
attributes.description: Net Present Value — the sum of all discounted future cash flows minus the initial investment cost, as output by the DCF model. A positive NPV indicates value creation above the required return. Populated for DCF approach type.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105; Argus Enterprise; FASB ASC 820

attributes.name: pgi
attributes.description: Potential Gross Income — the maximum annual rental revenue the property could generate at 100% occupancy at market rent. Used as the starting point for income capitalization approaches (direct cap and DCF). Populated for direct_cap and DCF approach types.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, 15th Ed.; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: physical_depreciation
attributes.description: Loss in value attributable to physical deterioration of the improvements, including curable deferred maintenance and incurable structural wear. Deducted from RCN in the cost approach. Populated for cost approach type.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105 — Cost Approach; Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, 15th Ed.

attributes.name: rent_basis
attributes.description: Basis on which the concluded market rent is expressed. Indicates whether the rent is annual or monthly and the lease structure (NNN — Triple Net, gross, or modified gross) that underpins the income analysis.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; RESO Data Dictionary; NAR Lease Standards

attributes.name: replacement_cost_new
attributes.description: Replacement Cost New (RCN) — the estimated cost to construct a building of equivalent utility using current materials, standards, and design at current prices. Starting point for the cost approach before depreciation deductions. Populated for cost approach type.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105 — Cost Approach; Marshall & Swift Valuation Service; RSMeans Cost Data

attributes.name: sensitivity_notes
attributes.description: Narrative description of key sensitivity scenarios tested for this approach, such as the impact of a 25 bps change in CAP rate or discount rate on concluded value. Supports investment decision-making and risk disclosure in appraisal reports.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105; Argus Enterprise Sensitivity Analysis; Appraisal Institute

attributes.name: terminal_cap_rate
attributes.description: Reversion or terminal CAP rate applied to the projected NOI in the final year of the hold period to estimate the property's residual (terminal) value in a DCF analysis. Typically higher than the going-in CAP rate to reflect future uncertainty. Populated for DCF approach type.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105; Argus Enterprise DCF Methodology; Appraisal Institute

attributes.name: total_opex
attributes.description: Total annual operating expenses (OPEX) for the subject property, including property taxes, insurance, management fees, maintenance, utilities, and reserves for replacement. Deducted from EGI to derive NOI. Populated for income capitalization approaches.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, 15th Ed.; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp recording the most recent modification to this valuation approach record. Used for change tracking, audit compliance, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 — Internal Controls; FASB ASC 820; ISO 55000 — Asset Management

attributes.name: vacancy_credit_loss_rate
attributes.description: Estimated rate (decimal fraction) applied to PGI to account for expected vacancy and uncollectible rent. For example, 0.05 represents a 5% vacancy and credit loss allowance. Used in income capitalization to derive EGI from PGI.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, 15th Ed.; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: weight_pct
attributes.description: Weighting factor (expressed as a decimal between 0 and 1) assigned to this approach in the final value reconciliation. For example, 0.60 indicates this approach contributes 60% to the concluded value. All approach weights for a given valuation should sum to 1.0.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105 §50 — Reconciliation; Appraisal Institute USPAP Standard 1

products.name: cost_approach
products.description: Cost approach valuation model record capturing land value, replacement cost new (RCN), depreciation components (physical deterioration, functional obsolescence, external obsolescence), depreciated cost of improvements, and concluded value via cost approach. Stores cost estimator reference, Marshall & Swift or RSMeans cost index used, effective age, economic life, remaining economic life, and land-to-value ratio. Used primarily for special-use properties, insurance valuations, and new construction assessments.

attributes.description: Professional designation held by the appraiser, such as MAI (Member Appraisal Institute) or SRA, confirming qualification level for the type of property being appraised. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MAI|SRA|AI-GRS|AI-RRS|FRICS|ASA|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute Designation Standards; USPAP Competency Rule

attributes.name: appraiser_license_number
attributes.description: State-issued license or certification number of the appraiser performing the cost approach valuation, required for regulatory compliance and credential verification per Appraisal Institute and USPAP standards.
attributes.references: USPAP Ethics Rule; Appraisal Institute Designation Standards; Title XI FIRREA

attributes.name: argus_model_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier or file name of the Argus Enterprise valuation model associated with this cost approach record, enabling traceability to the source cash flow and valuation model used in the broader appraisal engagement.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise (Valuation and Cash Flow Modeling); Appraisal Institute

attributes.name: chronological_age_years
attributes.description: The actual age of the improvements in years from the date of original construction to the valuation date. Provides context for comparing effective age and assessing the degree of deferred maintenance or renovation.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: condition_rating
attributes.description: Appraiser's qualitative rating of the physical condition of the improvements at the time of inspection, informing the observed condition depreciation analysis and supporting the effective age estimate.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate; USPAP Standards Rule 1-2(e)

attributes.name: cost_index_multiplier
attributes.description: Geographic and temporal adjustment multiplier applied to the base cost index to reflect local construction cost conditions at the subject property location and valuation date.
attributes.references: Marshall & Swift Valuation Service; RSMeans Local Cost Modifier

attributes.name: cost_index_source
attributes.description: The cost estimating publication or data source used to derive replacement cost new (RCN) figures, such as Marshall & Swift Valuation Service or RSMeans Construction Cost Data. Drives reproducibility and auditability of the cost estimate.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate; Marshall & Swift; RSMeans

attributes.name: cost_index_year
attributes.description: The publication year of the cost index edition (e.g., Marshall & Swift or RSMeans) used to establish the replacement cost new, ensuring temporal alignment with the valuation date.
attributes.references: Marshall & Swift Valuation Service; RSMeans Construction Cost Data

attributes.name: cost_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the cost basis used is replacement cost new (RCN — cost of a substitute improvement of equivalent utility using current materials and standards) or reproduction cost new (cost of an exact replica using original materials and design). Replacement cost is standard for most appraisals.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate; USPAP Standards Rule 1-4(b); IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this cost approach valuation record was first created in the system, providing an audit trail for data governance and SOX compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; FASB ASC 820; ISO 8601

attributes.name: depreciated_cost_of_improvements
attributes.description: The depreciated cost of improvements (DCI), calculated as replacement cost new less total accrued depreciation. Represents the contributory value of the improvements to the overall property value under the cost approach.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate; IVSC IVS 105 Para 50.4

attributes.name: depreciation_method
attributes.description: The methodology used to estimate total accrued depreciation, such as the age-life method, modified age-life method, observed condition method, or the breakdown method which separately quantifies each depreciation component.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, Chapter 17; IVSC IVS 105 Para 50.3

attributes.name: economic_life_years
attributes.description: The total estimated economic life of the improvements in years, representing the period over which the improvements contribute positively to property value. Used as the denominator in the age-life depreciation ratio.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, Chapter 17; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: effective_age_years
attributes.description: The appraiser's estimate of the age of the improvements in years based on observed condition and utility, which may differ from chronological age. Used in the age-life depreciation method to compute physical deterioration.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, Chapter 17; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: entrepreneurial_profit_pct
attributes.description: The market-derived profit percentage added to direct and indirect costs to reflect the entrepreneurial incentive and compensation for risk undertaken in developing the improvements, expressed as a percentage of total development cost.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate; IVSC IVS 105 Para 50.2

attributes.name: external_obsolescence_amount
attributes.description: Dollar amount of depreciation attributable to external (economic) obsolescence, reflecting loss in value caused by factors external to the property such as adverse market conditions, locational disadvantages, or environmental influences.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, Chapter 17; IVSC IVS 105 Para 50.3

attributes.name: functional_obsolescence_amount
attributes.description: Dollar amount of depreciation attributable to functional obsolescence, reflecting loss in value due to deficiencies or superadequacies in the design, layout, or utility of the improvements relative to current market standards.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, Chapter 17; IVSC IVS 105 Para 50.3

attributes.name: indicated_value
attributes.description: The concluded property value as indicated by the cost approach, calculated as land value plus depreciated cost of improvements plus site improvements value. This is the primary output of the cost approach model.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate; USPAP Standards Rule 1-6; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: inspection_date
attributes.description: The date on which the appraiser physically inspected the subject property to assess condition, quality, and improvements for the cost approach analysis.
attributes.references: USPAP Standards Rule 1-2(e); Appraisal Institute

attributes.name: insurance_replacement_value
attributes.description: The estimated cost to replace the insurable improvements (excluding land) at current prices without deduction for depreciation, used specifically for property insurance coverage determination. May differ from the cost approach indicated value.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; Marshall & Swift Insurance Valuation; ISO Property Insurance Standards

attributes.name: land_to_value_ratio
attributes.description: The ratio of land value to total indicated value via cost approach, expressed as a decimal. Used in portfolio analytics, tax assessment allocation, and insurance underwriting to assess the relative contribution of land versus improvements.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute; FASB ASC 805 (purchase price allocation); IRS Revenue Procedure

attributes.name: land_value
attributes.description: Estimated market value of the land component of the subject property as if vacant and available for its highest and best use, derived from comparable land sales analysis. A foundational input to the cost approach concluded value.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate; IVSC IVS 105 Para 50

attributes.name: land_value_method
attributes.description: The methodology used to estimate the land value component, such as sales comparison of vacant land, allocation from improved sales, or extraction. Documents the analytical basis for the land value conclusion.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, Chapter 11; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: methodology_notes
attributes.description: Narrative description of the appraiser's methodology, assumptions, limiting conditions, and any deviations from standard cost approach procedures. Supports IVSC-compliant methodology metadata and USPAP disclosure requirements.
attributes.references: USPAP Standards Rule 2-2(a)(viii); IVSC IVS 103; Appraisal Institute

attributes.name: physical_deterioration_amount
attributes.description: Dollar amount of depreciation attributable to physical deterioration of the improvements, including curable items (deferred maintenance) and incurable items (short-lived and long-lived components), derived from age-life or observed condition analysis.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, Chapter 17; IVSC IVS 105 Para 50.3

attributes.name: quality_rating
attributes.description: Appraiser's qualitative rating of the construction quality of the improvements, used to select the appropriate cost class and quality multiplier from the cost index (e.g., Marshall & Swift quality class). Drives the RCN per square foot selection.
attributes.references: Marshall & Swift Valuation Service Quality Classes; Appraisal Institute

attributes.name: rcn_per_sqf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Replacement Cost New Per Square Foot (RCN PSF)
attributes.description: Estimated cost to construct a replica or substitute improvement of equivalent utility at current prices, expressed on a per-square-foot (PSF) basis, derived from the selected cost index and adjusted for location and quality.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate; Marshall & Swift; RSMeans

attributes.name: rcn_total
attributes.description: Total replacement cost new (RCN) of all improvements, representing the estimated cost to construct a substitute improvement of equivalent utility at current prices. Computed as RCN PSF multiplied by gross building area, inclusive of direct and indirect costs.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate; IVSC IVS 105 Para 50.1; Marshall & Swift

attributes.name: remaining_economic_life_years
attributes.description: The estimated remaining economic life of the improvements in years, calculated as total economic life less effective age. Indicates the remaining period of positive contribution to value and is used in investment underwriting and insurance assessments.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate; IVSC IVS 105; FASB ASC 360

attributes.name: report_date
attributes.description: The date on which the appraisal report containing the cost approach analysis was signed and issued by the certified appraiser.
attributes.references: USPAP Standards Rule 2-2(a)(ii); Appraisal Institute

attributes.name: report_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known appraisal report number or engagement reference code assigned by the appraiser or appraisal firm, used for cross-referencing with Argus Enterprise and source appraisal documents.
attributes.references: USPAP Standards Rule 2-2; Appraisal Institute

attributes.name: site_improvements_value
attributes.description: Estimated depreciated value of site improvements such as paving, landscaping, utilities, and fencing that are separate from the primary building improvements and land value.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate; Marshall & Swift

attributes.name: total_depreciation_amount
attributes.description: Total accrued depreciation applied to the replacement cost new, representing the sum of physical deterioration, functional obsolescence, and external obsolescence. Subtracted from RCN to derive the depreciated cost of improvements.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate, Chapter 17; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: total_depreciation_pct
attributes.description: Total accrued depreciation expressed as a percentage of replacement cost new, providing a normalized measure of overall improvement condition and obsolescence for benchmarking and trend analysis.
attributes.references: Appraisal Institute — The Appraisal of Real Estate; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this cost approach valuation record was most recently modified, supporting audit trail requirements and change tracking for financial reporting and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; FASB ASC 820; GDPR Article 5(1)(e)

attributes.name: valuation_date
attributes.description: The effective date as of which the cost approach value conclusion is applicable, representing the point-in-time market conditions used in the analysis. Distinct from the report date.
attributes.references: USPAP Standards Rule 1-2(b); IVSC IVS 101 Para 20.3; ASC 820

attributes.name: valuation_purpose
attributes.description: The intended use and purpose of the cost approach valuation, which governs the applicable standard of value and methodology. Common purposes include insurance replacement cost, financial reporting under ASC 820/IFRS 13, and acquisition underwriting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: insurance|financial_reporting|acquisition|disposition|financing|tax_assessment|litigation|internal_review — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: USPAP Standards Rule 1-2(b); IVSC IVS 101; ASC 820; IFRS 13

attributes.name: valuation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the cost approach valuation record, tracking progression from initial draft through certified completion or supersession by a revised analysis.
attributes.references: USPAP; IVSC IVS 101

Serves as the quantitative backbone for investment-grade valuations and acquisition underwriting.

attributes.name: acquisition_price
attributes.description: Total assumed purchase price of the property at the start of the hold period, used as the basis for LTV, equity multiple, and IRR calculations.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise Acquisition Cost Input; IVSC IVS 105; FASB ASC 805

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which this DCF model was formally approved by the designated reviewer or investment committee. Required for SOX audit trail and governance compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302; IVSC IVS 101; Internal Valuation Governance

attributes.name: argus_model_reference
attributes.description: Native model identifier assigned by Argus Enterprise to the source cash flow model file. Used to trace back to the originating Argus Enterprise model for audit and reconciliation.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise Valuation and Cash Flow Modeling Module

attributes.name: argus_model_version
attributes.description: Version label of the Argus Enterprise model file (e.g., v1.0, v2.3-final) to distinguish iterative revisions of the same model.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise Valuation and Cash Flow Modeling Module

attributes.name: avg_dscr
attributes.description: Average annual Debt Service Coverage Ratio across the hold period, calculated as NOI divided by annual debt service. Lenders typically require a minimum DSCR of 1.20x–1.25x.
attributes.references: CMBS Underwriting Standards; Argus Enterprise DSCR Output; Federal Reserve Regulation Y

attributes.name: capex_reserve_psf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) Reserve Per Square Foot (PSF)
attributes.description: Annual capital expenditure reserve amount per square foot budgeted for building improvements, tenant improvements (TI), and leasing commissions over the hold period.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise CAPEX Reserve; NCREIF Capital Expenditure Standards; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this DCF model record was first created in the lakehouse Silver Layer. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; GDPR Article 5(e); Internal Data Governance

attributes.name: debt_amount
attributes.description: Total debt (mortgage or loan) assumed at acquisition used to finance the property purchase. Drives LTV and DSCR calculations within the model.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise Financing Assumptions; FASB ASC 470; CMBS/RMBS underwriting standards

attributes.name: discount_rate
attributes.description: The target Internal Rate of Return (IRR) used as the discount rate to compute Net Present Value (NPV) of projected cash flows. Reflects the required return on investment for this asset.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise Discount Rate Input; IVSC IVS 105; FASB ASC 820

attributes.name: equity_investment
attributes.description: Total equity capital contributed at acquisition, representing the difference between acquisition price and debt financing. Used to compute levered IRR and equity multiple.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise; ULI Real Estate Finance; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: equity_multiple
attributes.description: Total equity distributions (cash flows plus net reversion proceeds) divided by total equity invested. An equity multiple of 2.0x means the investor doubles their equity over the hold period.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise; ULI Real Estate Finance; NCREIF Performance Measurement

attributes.name: expense_growth_rate
attributes.description: Assumed annual percentage increase in operating expenses (OPEX) applied across the projection period. Typically benchmarked to CPI or market inflation indices.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise Expense Growth Input; BLS CPI; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: going_in_cap_rate
attributes.description: The capitalization rate implied by the acquisition price and Year 1 NOI. Used to benchmark the entry pricing against market comparables and assess acquisition risk.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise; Appraisal Institute; CoStar Market Analytics; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: hold_period_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which the modeled investment hold period ends, representing the assumed disposition or reversion date.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise Hold Period Parameter; IVSC IVS 105; ULI Real Estate Finance

attributes.name: hold_period_start_date
attributes.description: The date on which the modeled investment hold period commences, typically the assumed acquisition or ownership transfer date.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise Hold Period Parameter; IVSC IVS 105; ULI Real Estate Finance

attributes.name: hold_period_years
attributes.description: Total duration of the modeled investment hold period expressed in whole years (e.g., 10 for a 10-year hold). Drives the number of annual cash flow projection periods.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise; IVSC IVS 105; ULI Real Estate Finance

attributes.name: is_levered
attributes.description: Indicates whether this DCF model incorporates debt financing (levered analysis). True = levered model with debt service; False = unlevered all-equity model.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise Financing Toggle; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: levered_irr
attributes.description: The Internal Rate of Return computed on levered (equity) cash flows after debt service. Reflects the actual return to equity investors accounting for financial leverage.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise IRR Output; IVSC IVS 105; CFA Institute Real Estate Valuation

attributes.name: ltv_ratio
attributes.description: Ratio of the debt amount to the acquisition price at the time of underwriting, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.65 for 65% LTV). Key metric for lender and investor risk assessment.
attributes.references: CMBS/RMBS Underwriting Standards; FASB ASC 310; Federal Reserve Regulation Y

attributes.name: methodology_standard
attributes.description: The governing valuation methodology standard applied in constructing this DCF model. Ensures compliance with applicable appraisal and financial reporting frameworks.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105; Appraisal Institute USPAP; RICS Red Book; FASB ASC 820

attributes.name: min_dscr
attributes.description: The lowest annual DSCR observed across all projection periods in the hold period. Identifies the most stressed year for debt coverage, critical for lender covenant compliance.
attributes.references: CMBS Underwriting Standards; Argus Enterprise DSCR Output; Federal Reserve Regulation Y

attributes.name: model_assumptions_narrative
attributes.description: Free-text narrative documenting the key assumptions, market conditions, data sources, and qualifications underlying this DCF model. Required for IVSC-compliant methodology disclosure and investment committee review.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 101 Clause 20.4; Appraisal Institute USPAP SR 2-2; SEC Regulation S-X

attributes.name: model_number
attributes.description: Human-readable business identifier for this DCF model record, formatted as DCF-YYYY-NNNNNN. Used in investment committee presentations, audit trails, and cross-system references.
attributes.references: Internal Valuation Governance Standard; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: model_purpose
attributes.description: Business purpose for which this DCF model was constructed. Determines the applicable methodology standards and reporting requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: acquisition_underwriting|disposition_analysis|refinancing|annual_valuation|portfolio_reporting|impairment_testing|loan_origination — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105; FASB ASC 820; SEC Regulation S-X

attributes.name: model_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the DCF model record. Controls which version is authoritative for investment decisions and financial reporting.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 101; FASB ASC 820; Internal Valuation Governance

attributes.name: net_reversion_proceeds
attributes.description: Gross reversion value less estimated selling costs, representing the net cash inflow to the investor upon disposition at the end of the hold period.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise; IVSC IVS 105; ULI Real Estate Finance

attributes.name: npv_at_discount_rate
attributes.business_glossary_term: Net Present Value (NPV) at Discount Rate
attributes.description: Net Present Value of all projected cash flows (including reversion) discounted at the model's target discount rate. Positive NPV indicates value creation above the required return threshold.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 105; FASB ASC 820; Argus Enterprise NPV Output

attributes.name: rent_growth_rate
attributes.description: Assumed annual percentage increase in market rents applied across the projection period. Drives revenue escalation in the DCF cash flow schedule.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise Rent Growth Input; CoStar Market Analytics; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: reversion_value
attributes.description: Estimated gross sale proceeds at the end of the hold period, calculated by applying the terminal cap rate to the projected NOI in the reversion year. Represents the largest single cash inflow in the DCF model.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise Reversion Value; IVSC IVS 105; Appraisal Institute

attributes.name: selling_costs_rate
attributes.description: Percentage of reversion value deducted for estimated disposition costs (brokerage commissions, transfer taxes, legal fees) to arrive at net reversion proceeds.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise Selling Costs Parameter; IVSC IVS 105; NAR Commission Standards

attributes.name: sensitivity_irr_high
attributes.description: Levered IRR under the upside/bull case sensitivity scenario, reflecting optimistic assumptions (lower vacancy, higher rent growth, lower cap rate). Bounds the investment return range.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise Sensitivity Analysis; IVSC IVS 105; ULI Investment Analysis

attributes.name: sensitivity_irr_low
attributes.description: Levered IRR under the downside/bear case sensitivity scenario, reflecting stressed assumptions (higher vacancy, lower rent growth, higher cap rate). Used in investment committee risk analysis.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise Sensitivity Analysis; IVSC IVS 105; ULI Investment Analysis

attributes.name: stabilized_noi
attributes.description: Projected NOI at stabilized occupancy, representing the normalized income potential of the property once lease-up or repositioning is complete. Used for terminal cap rate application.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise; Appraisal Institute; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: terminal_cap_rate
attributes.description: The capitalization rate applied to the final year Net Operating Income (NOI) to derive the reversion/terminal value at the end of the hold period. Critical assumption in DCF reversion calculation.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise Terminal Cap Rate; Appraisal Institute; IVSC IVS 105

attributes.name: unlevered_irr
attributes.description: The Internal Rate of Return computed on unlevered (all-equity, pre-financing) cash flows. Measures the intrinsic return of the asset independent of capital structure.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise IRR Output; IVSC IVS 105; CFA Institute Real Estate Valuation

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this DCF model record was most recently modified. Used to detect stale models and enforce model refresh policies.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; GDPR Article 5(e); Internal Data Governance

attributes.name: vacancy_rate_assumption
attributes.description: Blended vacancy and credit loss rate applied to Potential Gross Income (PGI) to derive Effective Gross Income (EGI) in the model. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.05 for 5%).
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise Vacancy Input; Appraisal Institute; CoStar Market Analytics

attributes.name: valuation_date
attributes.description: The effective date as of which the DCF model value conclusion is stated. This is the principal real-world event date for the model, distinct from the model creation or approval date.
attributes.references: IVSC IVS 101 Clause 20.3; Appraisal Institute USPAP; FASB ASC 820-10-35

attributes.name: year1_noi
attributes.description: Projected Net Operating Income for the first year of the hold period, representing Effective Gross Income (EGI) less operating expenses. Foundational input for going-in cap rate and debt sizing.
attributes.references: Argus Enterprise NOI Projection; IVSC IVS 105; NCREIF Income Definition
